problem: Anyone can set the query parameter `?debug=true`. When it is set, the middleware skips the token check and sets g.user to an admin, so authentication is fully bypassed.
failure: Send `GET /any/protected/route?debug=true` with no X-Auth-Token header. The middleware sets g.user={'id':0,'role':'admin'} and returns without reaching abort(401), so an anonymous caller gets admin access in every environment.
fix: Remove the debug branch. If a debug login is truly needed, allow it only when an explicit non-production config flag is set, never from request input.

problem: The early `return` breaks the rule that every request passing the middleware has a validated X-Auth-Token. On the debug branch, the 401 path is never reached.
failure: With `?debug=true`, the request never reaches load_user or abort(401). Downstream handlers that trust g.user (role checks, audit logs keyed on id) see a made-up admin with id 0 that matches no real account.
fix: Remove the early-return branch so that every request goes through token validation before g.user is set.
